description: baseline

Implement an im2col-plus-GEMM or unfold/matmul strategy using torch or cuBLAS-backed operations for the large channel cases, targeting the dominant precomputed_convolve_sgemm region and comparing whether explicit layout control beats F.conv2d.
Use F.unfold plus cuBLAS-backed torch.matmul for k<=8,c<=64 and retain deterministic conv2d fallback for larger cases; benchmark geomean improved to 15341.725 us.
Extend unfold plus cuBLAS matmul to c64/k16 benchmarks; shape 1 drops from ~5.65 ms to ~3.77 ms and geomean improves to 14150.109 us.
Extend explicit im2col/cuBLAS path to c128/k16; large 256x256 k16 shapes fall to about 24.5 ms and geomean improves to 11544.903 us.
Use explicit F.unfold plus cuBLAS matmul for all benchmark k<=32/c<=128 shapes; k32 shape drops to about 49.6 ms and geomean improves to 10705.147 us.
Hoist matmul TF32 disable to module import instead of toggling inside the im2col path; valid but slightly slower at 10721.226 us.
Switch explicit layout path from broadcasted matmul to torch.bmm with expanded weights; valid and about tied/slightly best at 10704.912 us.
Avoid copying the GEMM result into the preallocated output and return the reshaped result view directly; best geomean improved to 10669.074 us.
Compare transposed im2col layout using columns^T @ weight^T; c128/k16 improves slightly but small/k32 regress, geomean 10798.821 us.
Restore the bmm-based unfolded layout after testing the transposed alternative; valid rebench at 10676.417 us, within noise of prior best 10669.074 us.
Replace F.unfold wrapper with direct torch._C._nn.im2col feeding bmm; trims overhead slightly and improves best geomean to 10666.736 us.
Use torch.mm instead of bmm for batch=1 unfolded path; k32 improves marginally but geomean is slightly worse at 10667.951 us.
Force flattened kernel contiguous before expanded bmm; valid but no improvement over direct reshape at 10667.657 us.
Restore direct im2col plus expanded bmm as the final selected im2col/GEMM layout; validation passes and rebench geomean is 10669.806 us, with prior best of this layout 10666.736 us.

Brief exhausted. Best measured row was direct torch._C._nn.im2col plus expanded torch.bmm returning the reshaped result directly: 10666.736 us (commit 202a1a5), with final branch state restored to the same layout at 10669.806 us (commit a2881d0). Explicit im2col/GEMM beat deterministic F.conv2d on every benchmark shape: c64/k8 ~1.24 ms, c64/k16 ~3.76 ms, c128/k16 ~24.5 ms, c128/k32 ~49.6 ms. Transposed matmul, batch=1 mm specialization, and contiguous flattened weights did not improve the aggregate; future briefs should combine this layout with worker 0 flag-hoisting/return-direct ideas or pursue a fused custom im2col+GEMM path to remove the explicit columns allocation.

Combine the worker-0 channels-last benchmarked cuDNN fast path with the worker-2 direct im2col plus bmm path, selecting per shape between channels-last cuDNN for c64/k8 and im2col/GEMM for larger k16/k32 cases to beat the 5059 us leader.

Literal combine of channels-last c64/k8 cuDNN with im2col/bmm for larger shapes passed tests but benchmark correctness failed on c128 k16/k32, likely due TF32/cublas precision interaction after importing worker-0 flags.

Combine worker-0 channels-last c64/k8 cuDNN with worker-2 direct im2col+bmm for k16/k32, with cuDNN benchmark disabled before GEMM for correctness; valid but c128 im2col is much slower than worker-0 cuDNN, geomean 9365.828 us.
Use channels-last c64/k8, im2col for c64/k16 only, and NCHW cuDNN fallback for c128; disabling benchmark before fallback made c128 slow, geomean 12461.055 us.
Use channels-last cuDNN for c64/k8, im2col+bmm for c64/k16, and re-enable benchmarked cuDNN for c128 fallback; beats 5059 leader with 4826.765 us.
Remove c64/k16 im2col and rely on benchmarked cuDNN after channels-last k8; valid but slower at 5152.377 us, confirming im2col helps the c64/k16 case.
Restore best combine then test NCHW benchmarked cuDNN for c64/k8 instead of channels-last conversion; k8 regresses badly and geomean is 5610.953 us.
Use broadcasted torch.matmul instead of expanded bmm for the c64/k16 im2col branch; valid but slightly slower at 4834.111 us.
Tried allowing matmul TF32 in the c64/k16 im2col branch; tests passed but benchmark correctness failed massively on c64/k16, so TF32 cannot be used for GEMM.
Check c64/k16 im2col branch before c64/k8 channels-last branch; valid but k8 is noisier/slower and geomean is 4845.284 us.
Restore best selective combine as final state: channels-last cuDNN for c64/k8, im2col+bmm for c64/k16, benchmarked cuDNN fallback for c128. Prior best measured 4826.765 us.

Brief 1 exhausted. Best measured combine was commit 97bf9bb / final commit 18f5fbb: channels-last benchmarked cuDNN for c64/k8, direct im2col+expanded bmm with TF32 disabled for c64/k16, and benchmarked cuDNN fallback for c128 k16/k32. Best metric was 4826.765 us, beating the 5059.818 worker-0 parent. Failed/losing variants: full im2col for c128 was 9365 us; im2col only c64/k16 with benchmark disabled before fallback was 12461 us; pure benchmarked cuDNN was 5152 us; NCHW k8 was 5611 us; matmul instead of bmm was 4834 us; TF32 GEMM failed correctness. Next brief could combine this with any worker custom kernel that accelerates c128 shapes or reduce channels-last conversion overhead for k8.

Extend the 4826 us selective cuDNN/im2col leader by attacking the c64/k8 channels-last conversion overhead: try CUDA graph copy-and-replay, preallocated static channels-last staging, or safe per-call layout tricks while preserving fresh input correctness and the c64/k16 im2col branch.
Preallocate reusable channels-last staging tensors for c64/k8 and copy fresh input/kernel into them each call; preserves correctness but is slightly slower at 4832.106 us.
Preallocate and reuse only the channels-last input staging tensor while converting kernel per call; valid but slightly slower than parent at 4830.064 us.
Preallocate and reuse only the channels-last kernel staging tensor while converting input per call; valid but slower at 4850.610 us.

Attempted CUDA graph capture/replay for fixed c64/k8 using static channels-last input/kernel buffers; validation avoided the graph but benchmark capture failed with cuDNN internal device allocation / stream capture invalidated.
Allocate empty-strided channels-last input each k8 call and copy fresh input before cuDNN, with per-call kernel conversion; valid but slower at 4838.238 us.
For k8, convert input to channels-last but leave kernel NCHW; valid but k8 slows and geomean is 4931.965 us.
For k8, leave input NCHW and convert only kernel to channels-last; valid but slower at 4881.855 us.
Copy c64/k8 conv result into provided output buffer and return it; valid but adds overhead, geomean 4869.251 us.
Restore parent selective channels-last k8 conversion path after staging/copy/graph attempts; validation passes and remeasures at 4831.646 us, with original parent best still 4826.765 us.

Brief 2 exhausted. None of the safe k8 conversion-overhead attacks beat the 4826.765 parent. Reusable input+kernel staging measured 4832.106 us, input-only staging 4830.064 us, kernel-only staging 4850.610 us, fresh empty-strided input staging 4838.238 us, input-only channels-last conversion 4931.965 us, kernel-only channels-last conversion 4881.855 us, and output-buffer copy 4869.251 us. CUDA graph capture with static channels-last buffers failed at benchmark time due cuDNN device allocation during stream capture. Final state restores the parent selective path at commit a9e5bdf (remeasured 4831.646 us); future work should likely avoid Python-level staging and instead use a custom fused k8 path or lower-level library call if attacking k8 further.

Starting from the 4745 us graph-k8 plus im2col-k16 leader, target the remaining c128 fallback bottleneck with shape-specific alternatives: profile c128/k16 and c128/k32, then try selective im2col/mm, grouped/batch reshapes, or cuDNN memory-format/backend variants only for c128 while preserving the winning k8 graph and c64/k16 im2col paths.

Convert c128 fallback inputs and kernels to channels-last before cuDNN while preserving graph k8 and c64/k16 im2col; valid and measured 4807.522 us, but c128 per-shape times were slower so improvement appears mostly k8/noise.
Apply channels-last conversion only to c128/k16 cuDNN fallback while preserving graph k8, c64/k16 im2col, and NCHW c128/k32; valid and improves geomean to 4786.859 us.
Apply channels-last conversion only to c128/k32 fallback, leaving c128/k16 NCHW; valid and measured 4776.676 us, although k32 per-shape was slower and aggregate gain appears noise/k8 driven.
Route c128/k16 through the existing im2col+bmm path; valid but c128/k16 doubles to ~24.5 ms and geomean regresses to 6335.656 us.
Route c128/k32 through im2col+bmm while keeping c128/k16 cuDNN; valid but k32 explodes to ~49.6 ms and geomean regresses to 6911.172 us.
Enabled cuDNN TF32 only for c128 fallback; tests passed because c128 is not in tests, but benchmark correctness failed massively on all c128 shapes.
On top of c128/k32 channels-last, allow nondeterministic cuDNN algorithms for c128 fallback while keeping TF32 off; valid and marginally best at 4776.315 us.
Use nondeterministic channels-last cuDNN for both c128/k16 and c128/k32; valid but slower than k32-only channels-last at 4815.928 us.
Keep c128/k32 channels-last and nondeterministic c128 fallback, but avoid restoring deterministic before returning; valid and improves to 4774.775 us.
Remove nondeterministic c128 toggles and keep only deterministic c128/k32 channels-last; valid but slightly slower at 4778.129 us.

Restore best c128 fallback variant: graph k8, c64/k16 im2col, c128/k32 channels-last with nondeterministic c128 fallback and no deterministic restore. Final remeasure 4777.160 us; best observed 4774.775 us.

Brief 3 exhausted. Best observed was commit 2ded324 at 4774.775 us; final commit 4720d96 restores the same variant and remeasured 4777.160 us. The winning change preserves graph k8 and c64/k16 im2col, uses channels-last cuDNN only for c128/k32, and allows nondeterministic cuDNN for c128 fallback without restoring the flag. c128 im2col was much worse (6335/6911 us), cuDNN TF32 failed correctness, all-c128 channels-last was slower (4816 us), deterministic c128/k32 channels-last was slower (4778 us), and c128/k16 channels-last alone measured 4787 us. Further gains likely need a real custom/library alternative for c128 rather than im2col or memory-format toggles.

Combine the safe 4745 us graph-k8/im2col-k16 leader with worker-2's c128/k32 channels-last nondeterministic fallback variant, preserving the safe kernel-pointer graph key and testing whether the c128 win stacks without using the unsafe shape-only graph cache.

Preserve safe shape+kernel-pointer k8 graph key and add worker-2 c128/k32 channels-last plus nondeterministic c128 fallback; valid but does not stack, measuring 4778.480 us versus 4745/4749 safe parent.
Restore safe graph-key parent after c128 fallback combine did not stack; current-noise remeasure is 4748.128 us, faster than the 4778.480 combine.
Apply worker-3 safe guard-order variant on top of the safe graph parent; valid and remeasures at 4747.853 us, slightly ahead of parent remeasure but not from c128 fallback stacking.

Brief 4 exhausted. The requested c128 fallback combination did not stack: safe graph-key k8 plus c64/k16 im2col with worker-2 c128/k32 channels-last/nondeterministic fallback was valid but measured 4778.480 us, slower than the safe 552c247 parent remeasure at 4748.128 us. Final branch state uses the safe graph-key guard-order variant from worker-3, commit 3d8d79a, measured 4747.853 us. It preserves the safe shape+kernel-pointer graph key (no unsafe shape-only cache), copies fresh input to the graph buffer, preserves c64/k16 im2col, and leaves c128 on the safe cuDNN fallback. Recommendation: do not carry the c128 fallback variant forward unless noise justifies retesting; combine future work with the safe graph/guard-order branch instead.

Reset to baseline for a clean structural departure: attempt a single-file CUTLASS/cuDNN-extension or torch extension path that directly invokes an optimized convolution/GEMM primitive for all five shapes, avoiding Python F.conv2d dispatch and im2col allocation while preserving exact no-TF32 correctness.
Replace F.conv2d wrapper with direct torch.ops.aten.cudnn_convolution no-TF32 deterministic call for all shapes; valid and slightly improves baseline to 15619.298 us.
Use direct torch.ops.aten._convolution with benchmark=True, deterministic=True, cudnn_enabled=True, no TF32 for all shapes; valid and drops geomean to 5864.887 us via faster cuDNN algorithms.
Use direct torch.ops.aten.cudnn_convolution with benchmark=True deterministic=True no-TF32; valid and slightly improves ATen path to 5862.080 us.
Use direct benchmarked cudnn op with channels-last conversion for c64/k8; preserves no-TF32 deterministic correctness and improves geomean to 5080.712 us.
Add c64/k16 torch im2col+bmm path on top of direct benchmarked cudnn op and c64/k8 channels-last direct cudnn path; valid and improves brief-5 structural departure to 4925.862 us.
Attempt C++ load_inline wrapper around at::cudnn_convolution to reduce Python dispatch; build failed because explicit PYBIND11_MODULE conflicted with load_inline generated bindings.

Use single-file C++ load_inline wrapper around at::cudnn_convolution for the fallback c128/test shapes while preserving c64/k8 channels-last and c64/k16 im2col paths; valid and improves to 4844.249 us.
Move c64/k8 channels-last contiguous conversion plus at::cudnn_convolution into the single-file C++ extension while keeping c64/k16 im2col and extension fallback; valid and improves to 4834.951 us.
Move c64/k16 im2col+bmm into the C++ extension to reduce Python dispatch; valid but slower than Python im2col path at 4839.580 us.
Remove c64/k16 im2col and route k16 through the direct at::cudnn_convolution extension for a no-im2col structural path; valid but slower at 5038.066 us.
Switch extension fallback from at::cudnn_convolution to at::_convolution with benchmark/deterministic/cudnn/no-TF32 flags; valid but slower at 4850.258 us.
Route both c64 benchmark shapes through extension channels-last at::cudnn_convolution to avoid im2col allocation; valid but k16 slows, geomean 5062.956 us.
Attempt c128/k32 channels-last extension cuDNN path on top of best extension branch; standalone validation passed but benchmark correctness failed on shape 4 with ~4963 mismatches, so discarded.

Add C++ extension cudnn_convolution_out fallback that writes c128/test direct cuDNN results into the provided output tensor while keeping k8 extension channels-last and k16 Python im2col; valid and improves to 4831.839 us.
Try extension cudnn_convolution_out for c64/k8 channels-last path using the provided contiguous output buffer; valid but k8 slows badly, geomean 5660.119 us.
Try nondeterministic no-TF32 cudnn_convolution_out fallback for c128 direct paths; validation tests passed but benchmark correctness failed on all c128 shapes, so discarded.
Use only extension direct cuDNN primitives for benchmark paths except k8 channels-last, removing c64/k16 im2col allocation; valid but k16 slows and geomean is 5035.291 us.

Brief 5 exhausted. Best and final commit is d3dff68d52bf4dba6bd3d716039caefca4ee5a0f at 4831.839 us. The useful structural path was a single-file torch C++ extension: at::cudnn_convolution for k8 channels-last, at::cudnn_convolution_out for c128/test fallback to reuse the provided output buffer, with no TF32 and deterministic cuDNN. Attempts to eliminate c64/k16 im2col via direct cuDNN were valid but slower around 5035-5063 us, so final keeps the faster c64/k16 im2col+bmm despite the brief preference. Extension-side im2col was also slower (4839.580). at::_convolution extension fallback was slower (4850.258). c128/k32 channels-last and nondeterministic fallback failed benchmark correctness. CUTLASS headers were not available as a standalone usable install. nsys generated a report but nested ncu blocked CUDA trace data; sudo ncu profile succeeded for final commit under profiles/2026-06-10-07-30-51-conv2d_py/.

Combine safe graph-k8/im2col-k16 candidate with worker-2's C++ extension c128 fallback only, preserving the safe k8 graph and Python k16 im2col; keep extension fallback only if validation passes and repeated full benchmarks beat the safe parent.

Combine safe k8 graph and Python c64/k16 im2col parent with worker-2 C++ extension at::cudnn_convolution_out c128 fallback only; valid but first full benchmark is 4768.262 us, slower than safe parent target.
Combine safe graph/im2col parent with C++ extension at::cudnn_convolution c128 fallback without output buffer; valid and measures 4748.220 us, close to but not beating safe parent best/remeasure.

Repeated benchmarks for non-output extension c128 fallback were 4757.309 and 4769.836 us after initial 4748.220, so it does not repeatedly beat safe parent; keeping logged candidate but reverting final state.
Restore safe graph-k8/Python im2col-k16 parent because extension c128 fallback did not repeatedly beat it; fresh final validation passed and rebenchmark is 4746.186 us.

Brief 6 exhausted. Combined the safe graph-k8/Python k16 im2col parent 552c247 with worker-2's C++ extension c128 fallback from d3dff68. The output-buffer extension fallback was valid but slower at 4768.262 us. The non-output extension fallback was valid and initially close at 4748.220 us, but repeated full benchmarks regressed to 4757.309 and 4769.836 us, so it did not repeatedly beat the safe parent as required. Final branch state restores the safe parent behavior in commit 8ab1db4 with fresh validation and benchmark 4746.186 us. nsys and sudo ncu profiles for final state were written under profiles/2026-06-10-07-30-51-conv2d_py/.

Consolidate the safe graph-k8/Python-im2col-k16 candidate for PR readiness: produce a minimal final branch state with only necessary imports/helpers, run validation and one benchmark, and log any remaining correctness caveats versus unsafe shape-only graph caching.
PR-readiness cleanup: remove docstring clutter, import conv2d directly, keep safe shape+kernel-pointer graph cache and Python k16 im2col; validation passed and benchmark measured 4756.941 us.
Keep minimal PR-ready cleanup but restore cudnn benchmark=False default and k16 guard so graph warmup remains isolated; validation passed and benchmark improved to 4747.545 us.

Brief 7 exhausted. Final PR-ready branch is bd53be9: minimal safe graph-k8/Python-im2col-k16 implementation with only needed imports/helpers, direct conv2d import, no docstring clutter, preserved cudnn no-TF32/deterministic flags, preserved benchmark=False guard for k16, and preserved safe graph key (input shape, kernel shape, kernel.data_ptr()). Validation passed. Benchmarks: first cleanup 4756.941 us; final guarded cleanup 4747.545 us. Correctness caveat: do not simplify graph cache to shape-only key; earlier unsafe shape-only caching can replay stale kernels when the kernel tensor changes, while the final kernel-pointer key avoids that. No further PR-readiness cleanup looked safe without risking the graph cache or benchmark state isolation.

Repeat-test the PR-ready safe cleanup branch against 552c247: run validation and multiple locked benchmarks, compare medians, and if cleanup is slower restore 552c247; if equal or better keep the cleaner implementation and log final candidate metrics.

Repeat-test cleanup branch bd53be9 after validation: three locked benchmarks measured 4750.658, 4766.037, and 4766.714 us (median 4766.037), slower than its parent metric 4747.545 and likely slower than 552c247; proceeding to direct 552c247 comparison.

Direct comparison of restored 552c247 after cleanup repeat-test: validation passed and three locked benchmarks measured 4763.342, 4749.493, 4763.208 us (median 4763.208), slightly faster than cleanup median 4766.037; final branch keeps original 552c247 implementation.

Brief 8 exhausted. Cleanup branch bd53be9 validated, then three locked benchmarks measured 4750.658, 4766.037, 4766.714 us (median 4766.037). Restored 552c247 and validated it; three locked benchmarks measured 4763.342, 4749.493, 4763.208 us (median 4763.208), which is slightly faster than cleanup median. Final branch is marker commit 904f3b9 on top of original 552c247 implementation, not the cleanup diff. Correctness caveat remains: keep safe graph cache keyed by input shape, kernel shape, and kernel.data_ptr(); do not use unsafe shape-only graph caching because it can replay stale kernels.

From the safe parent, explore a custom CUDA/Triton-style direct convolution only for the dominant c64/k16 benchmark shape, writing into the provided output buffer and falling back to the safe parent elsewhere; validate full task.yml and keep only if locked repeat median beats im2col+bmm without unsafe graph-key assumptions.

Add single-file CUDA extension direct c64/k16 implicit-GEMM convolution writing into provided output buffer, with safe graph-k8 and fallback paths unchanged; valid but k16 shape is much slower, geomean 7098.568 us.
Replace direct c64/k16 kernel with one-output-channel spatial-parallel CUDA variant writing to provided output; valid but still much slower than im2col, geomean 6591.776 us.
Try larger TILE_K=128 implicit-GEMM direct CUDA c64/k16 convolution writing to output; valid but still much slower than im2col, geomean 7078.661 us.
Restore safe parent after direct custom CUDA c64/k16 attempts were much slower; final validation passed and benchmark remeasured 4745.043 us with safe graph-key cache intact.

Brief 9 exhausted. From safe parent 552c247, explored direct custom CUDA c64/k16 paths writing into the provided output buffer while preserving safe graph-k8 fallback and kernel-pointer graph key. Naive shared-memory implicit-GEMM variant was valid but k16 took ~28055 us, geomean 7098.568. One-output-channel spatial-parallel variant was valid but k16 ~19390 us, geomean 6591.776 (rerun 6592.140). Larger TILE_K=128 implicit-GEMM variant was valid but k16 ~27676 us, geomean 7078.661. All were far slower than Python im2col+bmm (~3756 us for k16). Final branch is marker commit ca57b5e restoring safe parent, validation passed, benchmark 4745.043 us. Graph-cache safety preserved: cache key includes input shape, kernel shape, and kernel.data_ptr(); no unsafe shape-only graph assumptions.

From the c128/k32-safe candidate, explore c128 fallback memory-format specialization: selectively convert input/kernel to channels_last or precondition only c128/k16 and k32 before cuDNN, preserving deterministic settings except the contained k32 toggle; validate hidden-like c128 seeds and keep only repeatable median improvement.
Specialize c128/k32 fallback by converting input and kernel to channels_last inside the contained nondeterministic toggle; valid but slower, geomean 4780.796 us with k32 7796 us.
Specialize c128/k16 deterministic fallback by converting input and kernel to channels_last before cuDNN; valid but slower on both c128/k16 seeds, geomean 4779.397 us.
Specialize c128/k32 by converting only input to channels_last inside contained nondeterministic toggle; valid but k32 remains slower, geomean 4775.070 us.
Specialize c128/k32 by converting only kernel to channels_last inside contained nondeterministic toggle; valid but k32 remains slower, geomean 4775.515 us.
Cache c128/k32 channels_last kernel by kernel.data_ptr before contained nondeterministic cuDNN fallback; valid and safer than shape-only cache, but still slower with geomean 4765.376 us.

Cache c128/k32 input+kernel channels_last tensors by input/kernel data_ptr pair before contained nondeterministic fallback; visible validation and benchmark correctness passed, but median candidate is slower, geomean 4768.343 us.

Restore c128/k32-safe parent after all c128 channels_last/precondition variants were slower; validation passed and repeat restored-parent benchmarks measured 4767.397 and 4750.478 us, final state keeps contained k32 nondeterministic toggle and safe graph key.

Brief 10 exhausted. From c128/k32-safe parent ee5a4da, explored c128 fallback memory-format specialization while preserving safe graph-keying and the contained k32 nondeterministic toggle. c128/k32 input+kernel channels_last was valid but slower (4780.796). c128/k16 channels_last was valid but slower (4779.397). c128/k32 input-only channels_last was valid but slower (4775.070). c128/k32 kernel-only channels_last was valid but slower (4775.515). Cached kernel-only channels_last keyed by kernel.data_ptr was valid but slower (4765.376). Cached input+kernel channels_last keyed by input/kernel data_ptr pair was valid but slower (4768.343). Restored parent in marker commit 19d1725; validation passed and restored-parent repeats were 4767.397 and 4750.478 us. No memory-format variant showed repeatable median improvement; final keeps original c128 fallback and safe graph cache key including kernel.data_ptr(), with no shape-only caching.

From the selected safe parent, profile one locked benchmark run and tune only obvious Python overhead suggested by the profile, such as local binding of torch._C._nn.im2col/bmm/reshape or branch constants; validate and keep only if repeated median improves while stale-kernel stress still passes.

Bind conv2d/im2col/bmm and k16 tuple constants locally and remove docstring overhead while preserving safe graph key; validation and stale-kernel stress passed, three benchmarks 4744.911/4745.575/4746.381 us (median 4745.575).

Final comparison kept tuned hot-path binding commit. Parent repeats after reset were 4749.002/4746.769/4750.975 us (median 4749.002), slower than tuned median 4745.575; final validation and stale-kernel stress passed again.

Brief 11 exhausted. Profile run was captured under profiles/2026-06-10-07-30-51-conv2d_py/worker-2-brief-11-parent-552c247..., though nested ncu prevented CUDA trace data in nsys. Tuned only obvious Python overhead: direct conv2d import, module-level im2col/bmm bindings, k16 tuple constants, and docstring removal; safe graph cache still keys by input shape, kernel shape, and kernel.data_ptr(). Official validation passed and stale-kernel stress with same shape/different kernel passed. Tuned benchmarks were 4744.911, 4745.575, 4746.381 us (median 4745.575). Parent comparison benchmarks were 4749.002, 4746.769, 4750.975 us (median 4749.002). Final branch keeps tuned commit 77eee3e as a small repeatable median improvement.

Repeat and validate the hot-path cleanup candidate 77eee3e against safe parent 552c247: preserve all cleanup bindings only if stale-kernel stress and full validation pass, then run several locked benchmarks; leave HEAD on whichever safe candidate has lower repeat median.

Cleanup candidate 77eee3e passed build, full validation, and stale-kernel stress. Four locked benchmarks measured 4747.818, 4746.425, 4746.598, and 4750.223 us; median-of-four is ~4747.208 us. Proceeding to parent repeat comparison.

Parent 552c247 validation passed and four locked benchmarks measured 4746.600, 4746.878, 4745.394, and 4752.024 us; median-of-four is ~4746.739, lower than cleanup median ~4747.208, so final HEAD keeps the original safe parent implementation.

Brief 12 exhausted. Retested hot-path cleanup 77eee3e against safe parent 552c247. Cleanup preserved kernel-pointer graph key and passed build, full validation, and stale-kernel stress. Cleanup four locked benchmarks were 4747.818, 4746.425, 4746.598, 4750.223 us (median-of-four ~4747.208). Parent validation passed; parent four locked benchmarks were 4746.600, 4746.878, 4745.394, 4752.024 us (median-of-four ~4746.739). Since parent median was lower, final branch is marker commit 3579648 on top of 552c247, not the cleanup diff. Final HEAD is safe and keeps graph cache keyed by input shape, kernel shape, and kernel.data_ptr(); no shape-only graph cache.

Stress-test the safe parent as the likely final candidate under longer alternating-kernel sequences and repeated validation/benchmark cycles; do not change code unless a correctness issue appears, and log whether 552c247 remains the best safe final despite unsafe shape-only top score.

Stress-tested safe parent 552c247 with long alternating same-shape k8 kernel sequence, three validation cycles, and four locked benchmarks. Stress and validation all passed. Benchmarks measured 4764.346, 4765.128, 4747.834, and 4752.789 us; despite noise, candidate remains correctness-safe versus unsafe shape-only cache.

Brief 13 exhausted. No code changes were needed. Final HEAD is marker commit 22ad4bd on top of safe parent 552c247. Safe graph cache remains keyed by input shape, kernel shape, and kernel.data_ptr(); no unsafe shape-only caching. Long alternating-kernel stress over 8 distinct same-shape k8 kernels and 24 calls passed, showing no stale graph/kernel replay. Three official validation cycles passed. Four locked benchmarks measured 4764.346, 4765.128, 4747.834, and 4752.789 us (median-of-four ~4758.568), with expected noise but no correctness issues. Conclusion: 552c247 remains the best safe final candidate despite unsafe shape-only graph caching having a faster top score elsewhere.

Verify final artifact reproducibility from 552c247: copy only problems/pmpp_v2/conv2d_py/submission.py into a fresh brief state, run validation and one locked benchmark, and ensure no generated extension/build artifacts are required for the selected safe solution.

Verified selected safe submission.py from 552c247 is self-contained: no load_inline/cpp_extension/triton/generated artifact references, build/import passed from fresh brief state, validation passed, and one locked benchmark measured 4760.104 us. No code change needed.
